clue.text: Putting nearly everything on favourite is a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: on means the trimmed everything is placed after the favourite

parts.note: a favourite, like a teacher's pet, is a pet

indicators.note: nearly tells us to stop just short of the end of the word for everything

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes almost everything on the favourite and makes a costly blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, fitting the betting picture, but here it is a flower, and a bit of one is the definition. 'Nearly' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the parts of a flower, and a bloomer here means something in bloom.

clue.text: Stay upright, united with fellows in training

parts.note: an upright is a post, as in a goalpost

indicators.note: in places the words for united and fellows inside the abbreviation for training

parts.note: PT is physical training
united means made one
fellows means men

explanation.surface: Advice to hold a pole upright alongside colleagues during a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb, but it is a noun, as in a stay of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a delay or suspension of proceedings, a putting off to a later time.

clue.text: Annoyance coming from way in which one's promoted

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion moves the one, written I, higher up the word for way

parts.note: a trail is a path or way

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by the route that leads to their own promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is I; in TRAIL it moves up a place to give TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a source of irritation or trouble, as in a child who is a trial to their parents.

clue.text: Journal is going over habitual movements in organisation

parts.note: a log is a journal or record
tics are involuntary repeated movements

explanation.surface: A diary describes routine motions in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over' just places LOG above IS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Logistics is the detailed organisation and planning of a complex operation.

clue.text: Container for precipitation? There must be barrels around in area of course

indicators.note: in places the turned barrels inside the area of the golf course

parts.note: a tee is the area on a golf course where each hole starts

indicators.note: around asks for the word for barrels to be turned back to front

parts.note: butts are large barrels, as for water or wine

explanation.surface: Rain barrels needed on a golf course to catch the downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Precipitation looks like rain, but in chemistry a precipitate is formed in this glassware; 'around' reverses the barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist forms a precipitate in a small glass vessel; the question mark marks the play on rainfall.

clue.text: Wrong score put up for game

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
to score money is to net it

explanation.surface: An incorrect result is posted up for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Confirm spades, name held by suit

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades

indicators.note: held by puts the letter for name inside the word for suit

parts.note: a suit at law is an action

explanation.surface: Bridge players verify a call in spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a card suit beside spades, but it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to approve or ratify officially.

clue.text: Right time to break slab

indicators.note: to break the slab means time splits its letters

parts.note: a tile is a thin flat slab

explanation.surface: It's the proper moment to smash a paving stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a legal right or claim, as in title to a property.

clue.text: Common person from south embracing drunken folly in unattractive dive

indicators.note: embracing means the commoner's word wraps round the rest
from south means the word is read from the bottom up in this down entry

parts.note: a pleb is a common person

indicators.note: drunken signals a rearrangement of the letters of folly

explanation.surface: A tipsy commoner's foolish behaviour ends in an ugly plunge into the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From south' reads the commoner upwards in this down entry, and 'drunken' scrambles folly, which sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly flop is a clumsy dive landing flat on the stomach, the ugliest kind of entry.

clue.text: Agree to cover metal trap with fringes of green plant

indicators.note: to cover means the word for agree goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to settle is to agree, as on a price
tin is a metal
a gin is a snare or trap

indicators.note: fringes are the outside edges, so the first and last letters of green

explanation.surface: Accepting a plan to hide a metal snare among the edges of a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging nettle is a common weed with hairs that sting the skin.

clue.text: Haplessly stare, hard put to identify state of India

indicators.note: haplessly suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stares blankly, struggling to name an Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard put' looks like a phrase meaning struggling, but its letters are fodder with STARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state of India, in the north.

clue.text: Top hero's first unaccompanied in journey all round

indicators.note: all round means everything built so far is turned back to front
in puts the hero's initial and the word for alone inside the journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of hero's

parts.note: unaccompanied means solo

explanation.surface: The leading man goes solo on a round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' turns the whole assembly, journey with its filling, end to end, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo shirt is a garment worn on the upper body, which is what a top is.

clue.text: Anxious after loss of diamonds and platinum in country

indicators.note: loss of means the letter for diamonds is taken out

parts.note: edgy means anxious
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
Pt is the chemical symbol for platinum

explanation.surface: Someone nervous after losing their jewels and precious metal abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Tip and related piece of material giving consumer protection

definitions.text: piece of material giving consumer protection

parts.note: in racing a nap is a tipster's strongest tip
kin means related, as in kin to someone

explanation.surface: A tip about a fabric guard for shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer' looks like a shopper but means someone eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a cloth that protects a diner's clothes while eating.

clue.text: Evil, super being frenzied in defeat

indicators.note: something frenzied is in wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An evil superhero in a rage crushes their foes.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulverise an opponent is to defeat them utterly, crush them.

clue.text: Work in place I designed for ballet

indicators.note: in puts the word for work into the rearranged letters
designed suggests something arranged anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A creative piece arranged in a spot I planned for dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppelia is a comic ballet by Delibes; 'designed' scrambles the place and I, with the work set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppelia is a comic ballet by Delibes, about a doll that seems to come alive.

clue.text: Supreme head of allied force, old, aboard boat

indicators.note: aboard puts the other pieces inside the word for boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of allied

parts.note: to ram is to force

explanation.surface: An old commander of Allied forces sets sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means of supreme importance, above all else.

clue.text: Faithful follower, hot, joining mass in endless delight

indicators.note: in places the mass letter inside the trimmed word for delight
endless means the last letter of the word for delight is dropped

parts.note: to enchant is to delight

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter, flushed and joining the crowd, is endlessly thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts ENCHANT to ENCHAN, and M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a loyal supporter, often of a gang leader.

clue.text: In short time girls see what refinement can bring

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Girls at finishing school soon see the benefits of polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refinement' looks like good manners, but means sugar refining.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left over when sugar is refined.

clue.text: Support for new setter?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a new setter is a young dog of that breed, a puppy

explanation.surface: Encouragement for a fresh crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like a crossword compiler, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up is to support, as with a beam.

clue.text: Kick in playground crude?

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playground
crude is unrefined oil

explanation.surface: A rough boot of a ball in the park?
explanation.walkthrough: REC, a recreation ground, is a British word for a local park or playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Recoil is the kick of a gun when fired.

clue.text: Enormously revolutionary element beginning to dominate

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the element is read backwards

parts.note: neon is a chemical element

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of dominate

explanation.surface: A huge rebellious force starts to take over.
explanation.definitionFit: No end, as in it pleased me no end, means enormously or very much.

clue.text: Pipe inlaid with a piece of gold

indicators.note: inlaid with means the pipe has the a set into it

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or tube

explanation.surface: A tube decorated with a golden inlay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat is an old gold coin used across Europe.

clue.text: Soft drink, large quantities, ending outside

indicators.note: outside means the ending wraps round the large quantities

parts.note: a coda is a closing passage or ending
reams are large quantities, as of paper

explanation.surface: Gallons of a fizzy drink at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured fizzy drink.

clue.text: People of America having very big part in history

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for very big
an age is a period of history

explanation.surface: Americans with a huge role in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people, originally of the Ohio valley.

clue.text: Upset party rival, ignoring leader, keeping hairstyle

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: keeping means the trimmed rival holds the hairstyle
ignoring leader means the first letter of the word for rival is dropped

parts.note: to emulate is to rival
a bob is a short hairstyle

explanation.surface: A political opponent, leaderless, is put out but holds on to their haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but is a dance; 'ignoring leader' cuts EMULATE to MULATE, holding BOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To discombobulate is to confuse or disconcert, to upset someone.

clue.text: One watching conservationists in river and lake

indicators.note: in puts the conservationists inside the river

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: An observer spots environmentalists by a river and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard who keeps watch.

clue.text: In dispute, ethic's effectiveness

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Ethics in an argument and how effective they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth means power or effectiveness, as in a law with teeth.
